pr_body:
Replaces the custom `EntrypointInvoker` in favor of runtime's `call_assembly_entrypoint` which now supports `MainAsync`.

Fixes: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30600
Fixes: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/31148

issue_context.title: Replace EntryPointInvoker in Blazor WebAssembly with code in the runtime
issue_context.body: .NET WASM has an API to invoke the entry point: `mono_call_assembly_entry_point`. We previously used it, but moved away from it since it did not support `MainAsync` at that point.  This has since been fixed so there's no reason for us to continue using our implementation. Here's the PR that made the change: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/3a93704737cceb38c4d51ae03075cf4eaad81b23. We would essentially want to undo the source changes, but keep the tests.

review_comments: This should also resolve https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/31148 since it is getting rid of the last call to `Console` in a default Blazor WASM app.
Do we want to keep/tweak these tests to make sure things still work the same? Or are these behaviors/tests covered already elsewhere?
We have E2E tests validating this.

I don't believe these tests should be necessary any longer as they were meant to test out the functionality of the `EntrypointInvoker` specifically, which has now been removed. The core logic of finding the assembly and entrypoint is now handled on the runtime layer. Note; we do still have the E2E tests for the functionality: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Components/test/E2ETest/Tests/StartupErrorNotificationTest.cs
